Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Ιουνίου, «Αγια Βαρερια η Παρθενα», with the rank word left off. The day's line gives the second form beside it, «Βαρέρια (ή Βαλερία)», which is the one the folder's English name follows.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 7. јун ст. ст., „Свете мученице Кириакија, Велерија и Марија“, which names her second of three. Свете is not a rank and мученице is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, so both come off and the bare personal name is the whole of the form; the heading carries no place, the city being in the body. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM`, so this is the first holder.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 6 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day as the folder's Romanian row, and carries all five virgins on one page with a head line for each. The day's line gives this one two forms, «Βαρέρια (ή Βαλερία)», and the head line uses the first: «Αγια Βαρερια η Παρθενα». The other four of the five have no folder in the corpus and are drafted new in `el-06-06`. The page gives no year, no emperor and no judge's name, so the folder's dateless reading stands. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.06.2026 (7. јун ст. ст.) — „Свете мученице Кириакија, Велерија и Марија“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THREE OF A COMPANY OF FIVE, AND THE IDENTIFICATION IS ON THE STORY AND NOT ON THE NAME. saint.gr keeps five virgins of Caesarea in Palestine on 6 June in one line and on one page — Martha, Maria, Kyria (or Kyra), Vareria (or Valeria) and Markia — and this book keeps THREE of them on the 7 June. The story is the same sentence by sentence: Caesarea of Palestine; the withdrawal to one dwelling („у једну колибу“ against the Greek’s one house); unceasing prayer with fasting „да би се вера Христова распрострла по васцелом свету“ against «that the faith of the Christians might shine out over the whole world»; the betrayal, here a slander; and death under torments, one after another. **THE SOFT SPOT IS THE FIRST NAME AND IT IS NAMED HERE.** This book writes «Кириакија» where the Greek page writes «Κυρία» and glosses it «or Kyra»: a third variant of a name the Greek page already could not settle, and Kyriake is not Kyria letter for letter. **The identification rests on the company and the story — three women of Caesarea in one hut praying for the spread of the faith, betrayed and tortured to death — and not on the spelling**, and it is said so plainly here. MARTHA AND MARCIA GET NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE READING TOO: this book names three of the five and `martha-of-caesarea` and `marcia-of-caesarea` are not among them, so neither folder was touched. A company is what the heading enumerates. A FIRST DATE FOR ALL THREE. All five folders held `dates: null`, and `kyria-of-caesarea`’s life says why: saint.gr «gives no year for it and names no emperor». This book closes „мучене и мукама уморене 304. године“ — stated flat, of the three together, with no „око“. `death` 304 to 304, `basis` `traditional`. **Only on the three the heading names**; Martha and Marcia stay undated, which is the asymmetry the source itself makes. THE DAY WAS CHECKED, FOR THE FIFTH DAY RUNNING: `sr-cand.mjs 06-06` prints Bessarion, Hilarion the New and the three virgin martyrs Archelais, Thekla and Susanna, **and not these three**, so the 7 June is this book’s day for them and the row carries it although both other calendars keep the company on the 6th. `related` UNTOUCHED: all five folders already relate to the other four, written off the Greek page, and this entry names nobody else. No `locations` — Caesarea of Palestine is in both accounts and the folders have stayed unplaced. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **`virgin` ADDED ON THIS FOLDER ALONE, AND IT MOVES WHAT THE PAGE PRINTS.** This folder carried only `martyr`, because doxologia’s line gave the rank and nothing else and saint.gr’s page was read into the company’s other folders as «virgins»; `kyria-of-caesarea`, `maria-of-caesarea`, `martha-of-caesarea` and `marcia-of-caesarea` all carry `martyr` and `virgin` already. This book calls the three „ове славне девице“ in its closing sentence, which is §5’s Девица said of her outright. `PRECEDENCE` tests `martyr && virgin` for `virgin-martyr`, so the page will stop printing *Martyr Valeria (6 June)* and start printing *Virgin Martyr* — **which is what the other four of her company have always printed**, so the change makes the five consistent rather than odd. It is named because it moves a rendered rank, as the 3 June `martyr` on the Tsarevich was.

death.note: The folder had no dates: saint.gr gives the company no year and names no emperor, and doxologia's line for the one of the five it prints gives nothing either. The Охридски пролог for 7. јун ст. ст. states it flat, of the three women its heading names: „По некој клевети беху изведене на суд, мучене и мукама уморене 304. године“. No approximation and nothing to derive it from (5 October 2026).
